text:
ashley: kicked off canary for v2.3.1 at 23:10 PT. small-batch p99 is up ~18% vs yesterday's baseline. not a hard fail but crosses our soft threshold. tagging folks for quick triage. :eyes:

sam: on it. which workload/route? can you paste the perf snapshot?

ashley: route=/generate/small, batch_size=1-4 mostly. pasted initial snapshot below.

```
canary_id=canary-2026-17677
baseline_p99=98ms
canary_p99=116ms
baseline_p95=34ms
canary_p95=36ms
throughput=~220r/s
kv_cache_hit_rate=0.86
CPU_util_canary=67%
GPU_util_canary=44%
```

deploy-bot: Canary canary-2026-17677 started by @ashley at 2026-03-16T23:10:00Z

rui: I'll pull a 3-min flame on the canary instance and check for syscall stalls or scheduling blips. also will check the batching/kernel selection logs.

dean: quick thought — we changed the continuous-batching heuristics in the last patch (PR #4201). that could nudge latency for very small requests. I can revert that heuristic for just the canary if we want to test.

ashley: good call. if it's the batching heuristic, reverting should show improvement within a minute. can we run a quick AB: revert vs current?

sam: I can spin a patched canary (batching.heuristic=legacy) on another slot, r10, and run the same traffic for 5 min. will need permission to allocate one slot.

qa: tagging to run our small-batch smoke prompt set when the patched canary is ready. I'll schedule the job.

perf-bot: Alert: p99 delta +18% for /generate/small over 5m window. Threshold set at +15%.

rui: flame snapshot shows a small hotspot in the attention kernel for seq_len=64 where we dropped to a fallback kernel for a handful of calls. looking for correlation with kernel selector logs now.

ashley: commands I'm running for realtime checks:
```sh
curl -s "http://perf-api:9090/query?query=histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(latency_bucket[5m])) by (le))&route=/generate/small"
# and
ssh perf@canary-2026-17677 sudo journalctl -u runtime-service -n 200 --no-pager | tail -n 80
```

dean: I patched r10 with legacy heuristic. canary-r10 up. starting traffic replay now.

sam: replay running (id=replay-810). initial 2min: p99=102ms. better than canary-2026-17677 but still slightly above baseline.

rui: kernel selector logs show a transient mismatch: some requests with seq_len=64 were classified as long-leading, causing a slower attention fallback. looks like the new heuristic misclassifies when there are many short prefixes.

ashley: OK — that indicates root cause. options: 1) revert heuristic for rollout (safe), 2) quick patch to selector to refine prefix logic (risky), 3) let canary continue and monitor (not preferred).

dean: I recommend revert for now. I'll stage the revert to canary fleet. if r10 numbers hold, we roll forward with revert and open a follow-up to refine selector.

sam: agree. timeline?

dean: patch and redeploy to canary slots in ~5m, will post when done.

ashley: decision: HOLD rollout until canary p99 <= 110ms for 10 continuous minutes. if not, rollback. I'm putting a temporary hold on the runbook to auto-rollback; manual ack required. :hand:

perf-bot: Note: rollback automation paused for canary-2026-17677 by @ashley

sam: r10 stabilized: p99=100ms over last 6 min. continuing to monitor.

rui: CPU traces show less time in fallback kernel post-revert. kv cache hit rate unchanged. I think selector was misrouting calls to slower path.

qa: smoke set ran, no functional regressions observed. latency mark improved on patched canary.

ashley: thanks all. next steps: dean to roll revert across canary slots, sam to monitor p99 for 10m, if stable we will promote. if numbers degrade, rollback to previous stable commit and open hotfix. tagging @eng-runtime for postmortem to refine selector heuristics and add a gated unit test for prefix classification.

sam: ack — I'll prepare the promote plan and keep this thread updated.

ashley: one more ask — please dump one 30s tcpdump on canary-2026-17677 after your promote to verify no odd network retries. small chances but worth a check.

deploy-bot: Canary canary-2026-17677 reverted to batching.heuristic=legacy on slots [r10,r11,r12] at 2026-03-16T23:18:40Z

ashley: thanks. holding until end of 10m window. will update here with final decision. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
